name: Sida
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Badenoch, Nathan & Hayashi Norihiko. 2017. Phonological sketch of the Sida language of Luang Namtha, Laos. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 10(1): 1-15. hdl:10524/52394; open (CC-BY) copy DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15477086.
catalog_quote: The tone bearing unit in Sida is the syllable, not the word. Sida has three lexical tonemes: /55/ high, /33/ mid and /31/ low falling. Examples of tone contrast include: /i31tɕʰo31/ 'hat; mountain' /i55tɕʰo31/ 'water' ... /a55 pʰi31/ 'grandmother' /a31 pʰi55/ 'chili-hot' Additionally, there are two grammatical tones: /35/ mid-rising and /53/ high-falling. Grammatical tones can be considered tonal alternations caused by certain grammatical constructions. At this point we have identified three alternation patterns, although we believe more will emerge.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: Sida is a syllable-tone language with three lexical tones (55, 33, 31) and two grammatically induced tones (35, 53); every syllable carries a tone. The description contains no statement about word stress or accent at all; there is no sesquisyllabic or minor-syllable structure reported (canonical syllable C1(C2)V(C3)/T, tone on every syllable). Edmondson 2002 on the Vietnamese variety likewise reports three tones (35/31/33) and says nothing about stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated regarding stress. Tonal alternations: 31 to 35 on the second element of a noun-noun possessive (wa31ɲɤ35 sɯ31to31 'Sida language'), 31 to 33 before the possessive particle kɔ33, and 55/31 to 53 before the interrogative particle wa31 (pp. 6-7).
new_statements.domain_note: Word/syllable level; data are citation forms and short elicited phrases from four speakers of Ban Nam Dii, Luang Namtha, Laos.
new_statements.identity_note: Badenoch & Hayashi 2017 describe the Luang Namtha (Ban Nam Dii) dialect of Lao Sida; they report two further Phongsaly dialects (Lower: Samphanh/Bun Nuea; Upper: Nyot Ou) not described. Edmondson 2002 describes the Vietnamese Sila of Can Ho commune (Muong Te, Lai Chau). All are under the single glottocode sila1247 [slt]; no separate dialect glottocodes exist.

sources.note: Section 3.1 'Distinctive features of Sila' (pp. 5-6, Vietnamese Sila of Can Ho commune): initials, open rimes only, tones 35 (<*1), 31 (<*2), 33 (<*3), creaky closed syllables in compounds; no statement on stress for Sila. The single 'unstressed' remark (§2.2) concerns Cong vs Phunoi minor syllables, not Sila.
